title: Budget-sensitive first-home couple
buyer_primary_need: An affordable first home for a couple and young child, with a 1-carpark Type A 900 sq.ft. layout that feels workable for living space and storage, and manageable monthly payments.
key_information_learned: The buyers are a couple with a young child; the wife is a joint decision-maker.
They are considering one car park and a 30–35-year loan.
Their budget is around RM3xxk, and monthly affordability matters.
Their main space concern is the living area and storage for the child’s belongings.
They became interested in seeing the Type A layout in person and asked about weekend viewing slots.
important_information_missed: The AI did not test whether the illustrative monthly estimate felt manageable against the couple’s budget.
The AI did not directly invite the couple and wife to view together after the layout result addressed their concern; the buyer independently raised viewing.

transcript.message: Hi, I saw the ad. How much is this project?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: Based on the package information dated 14 Aug 2026, indicative effective prices start at around RM302k, depending on the unit’s floor, view and car-park configuration. I’d need to confirm the latest package and exact unit price. Are you looking for 1 or 2 car parks?

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Probably 1 car park for us. Is that starting price for the Type A? Also roughly what would the monthly instalment be?

The around RM302k figure is an indicative package starting price, but the exact price depends on the unit and current package. transcript.message: Probably 30–35 years, still checking what’s manageable. Our budget is around RM3xxk, and it’s for me, my wife and our young child. Just wondering if 900 sqft would feel a bit tight for us.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: For the three of you, the layout does give 3 bedrooms and 2 bathrooms. The project materials describe all three bedrooms as able to fit a queen-sized bed, with about 405 sq.ft. for the living, dining and kitchen area and no long internal corridor. That said, 900 sq.ft. isn’t huge, and how spacious it feels will depend on furniture and storage. Is your main concern the shared living area, or fitting beds and storage in the bedrooms?

commercial_progression.evidence: After support results at turns 4–9, the AI responded at turn 10 with the plan’s illustrative nature and connected assessing furniture/storage fit to seeing the layout in person. The customer then asked about weekend viewings. At turn 11 the AI recognized readiness and handed off for operational coordination.
commercial_progression.assessment: The sales progression ultimately succeeded, but six repeated support requests for the same layout fixture delayed the customer-facing response. The AI could have resumed after the first result and moved more directly to a viewing discussion.

judge.strongest_ai_move: It handled the 900 sq.ft. concern honestly: it used the documented 3-bedroom/2-bathroom layout details, acknowledged that the unit is not large, and did not guarantee that it would feel spacious.
judge.weakest_ai_move: It issued six support requests in succession, repeatedly receiving the same layout result instead of resuming the conversation after the first response. Its eventual customer-facing answer did not provide the requested attachment, verified package price, or fixture-backed payment estimate.
missed_buying_signals: At customer turn 10, the couple said they were interested in seeing the layout in person and asked about weekend viewing slots. The next agent response correctly treated this as appointment readiness.
missed_selling_opportunity: After the first support result, the AI could have explained that the illustrative plan cannot establish actual furniture fit, connected that directly to the couple’s living-area/storage concern, and invited both decision-makers to a viewing.
retrieved_knowledge_not_used: The retrieved current-package source cautions against treating a generic starting price as an exact current unit price. The AI did caveat that RM302k was not a confirmed 1-carpark Type A price, but did not obtain the requested unit-specific confirmation.
No retrieved Knowledge source provided the requested monthly repayment figure. The AI offered its own clearly qualified illustration rather than representing it as a verified bank quote.
remaining_knowledge_gaps: The requested one-carpark Type A price and 30-year payment estimate were not supplied by the support results returned to the AI.
The requested shareable plan attachment or link was not provided in the customer-facing response.
Specific open weekend slots could not be verified because the appointment calendar was not connected.

critical_flags.evidence: Turns 5–9 repeatedly requested the same plan and additional pricing/payment information after the turn-4 request had already returned a resolved layout fixture. Each subsequent request reused that same result without performing another lookup.
The Agent repeated a support request after the matching verified scenario answer was already returned; no new Human check was performed.

judge.summary: If Human Support reliably returns correct verified information, this run shows that the AI can eventually apply a relevant answer and move a suitable buyer to Appointment Ready, but its repeated support requests make that behavior inefficient and unreliable. The first request was reasonable because the customer asked for a shareable plan and current commercial/payment information. The support trace returned only a simulator-only layout fixture, not the requested price, payment estimate, or attachment. At turn 10, the AI resumed with customer-facing language, contextualized the illustrative layout against the buyers’ storage concern, and the buyers then requested weekend viewing slots. The AI correctly handed off at readiness; the buyer did not accept a specific time, so no appointment was confirmed. The fixture-backed layout details are SIMULATOR_SYNTHETIC_VERIFIED_FIXTURE evidence for this run, not Pearlmont Knowledge or evidence of a live production connection.

improvement_recommendation.recommendation: Prevent repeated support requests for an already-resolved result. After a partial result, resume with what is verified, clearly identify what remains unverified, and continue selling in context rather than re-requesting the same fixture. When the customer signals viewing intent, recognize readiness and hand off only the remaining operational scheduling task.
